title: Aztán, Utána: Telling a Funny Story

sections.title: Building toward the laugh
sections.content: A funny story leans on exactly the same aztán/utána chain you already use for any past narrative — the only real difference is where you put the surprise. Save the funniest detail for right after aztán, so the story builds toward it instead of giving it away up front.

sections.title: Building toward the laugh
rows: Petra elmesélt egy vicces történetet a munkahelyen.
Petra told a funny story at work.
Előbb csendben voltunk, aztán hangosan nevettünk.
First we were quiet, then we laughed loudly.
A vicc vicces volt, de egy kicsit nevetséges is.
The joke was funny, but also a little ridiculous.

items.spanish: Károly elmesélt egy viccet, és nagyon nevettünk.
items.english: Károly told a joke, and we laughed a lot.

items.spanish: Nevettem a viccén, aztán elmeséltem Károlynak is.
items.english: I laughed at his joke, then told Károly about it too.

items.spanish: A vicc nagyon vicces volt, ezért sokat nevettünk.
items.english: The joke was very funny, so we laughed a lot.

sections.content: The punchline works better last. Keep the setup short — one or two clauses with előbb or plain past tense — and let aztán introduce the funny part.
